newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Rising exports should boost Slovak output-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Rising exports should boost Slovak output-analysts.

text.p: Rising first quarter exports should boost Slovak industrial production figures for March, bringing output data in line with official forecasts, analysts said in a Reuters survey on Monday.
The Slovak Statistical Bureau (SUSR) is expected to release official data for industrial and construction output for March on Tuesday.
Analysts forecast output to grow some 2.0 to 4.0 percent in March, roughly equal with the SUSR's projection of average growth in the first quarter of 3.5 to 3.9 percent year-on-year.

"Given the fact that exports posted an interesting increase in the first quarter of the year, one can expect industrial production to grow some two to four percent in March," Milan Durech, a macroeconomic analyst at Tatra Banka, told Reuters.
Industrial output rose 2.2 percent in February after a 2.0 percent year-on-year increase in January.
Durech said he expected industrial output to maintain a two to four percent year-on-year growth until at least the end of the first half of 1996.
"But naturally on the condition that at the same time exports keep their upward trend," Durech added.
Slovakia's exports totalled 69.517 billion crowns in the first quarter, an increase of 12.2 percent over the same period in 1996.

Martin Barto, an analyst at ING Barings, said he expects an increase in industrial output of up to four percent in March but he did not see too much room for further acceleration in production due to continuing structural problems in the economy.
"There is no need to produce a larger amount of goods than we make and export at present," Barto said.

"From a longer term perspective, let us say in the first half of this year, I do not expect a further increase in industrial output since small and medium-sized companies still do not show the desired restructuring," he added.
Medium and small enterprises account for a major part of Slovakia's industrial production. There are 1,571 firms with up to 500 employees in Slovakia, out of a total of 1,723 registered companies.
